objective: Correct pi-commands and pi-catalog ownership by moving scaffold templates beside the scaffolder, splitting scaffold planning, rendering, and transactional application, and leaving pi-catalog focused on runtime discovery without changing generated bytes or public command behavior.

in: Characterize /scaffold parsing, completions, previews, generated bytes and paths, staging, commit/rollback, containment, symlink, collision, and error behavior for every supported kind.
Move extensions/pi-catalog/templates to extensions/pi-commands/templates with history-preserving renames.
Update template-root containment, TypeScript/resource/anatomy checks, documentation, tests, and generated inventory references.
Split the scaffolder into planning, rendering, and transactional application concerns while preserving its public surface.
Remove generation-template ownership and claims from pi-catalog while retaining runtime command/tool discovery.
out: Changing /scaffold names, supported kinds, target paths, generated bytes/paths, rollback behavior, or security guarantees.
Removing, disabling, or converting /scaffold primitive to deprecation-only behavior without an approved release-level compatibility revision.

constraints: After initiatives 01-03 establish provider and HUD boundaries, this initiative may proceed in parallel with 04-pi-swe-todo-separation and 05-pi-artifacts-publication-backend; it does not depend on their completion.
No runtime or test reference may remain to pi-catalog/templates after migration.
Golden previews and applied generated trees must remain byte-for-byte compatible for all scaffold kinds.
Preserve containment, symlink, collision, staging, commit, and rollback safety.
For this initiative set, retain /scaffold primitive unchanged; the consolidation plan's removal/deprecation step is explicitly deferred until a separately approved breaking-change revision.
Regenerate and verify catalog/gentic-inventory.json and related capability fixtures when paths/ownership change.

acceptanceCriteria.text: All scaffold templates are owned beneath pi-commands and no production, test, documentation, or inventory reference points to pi-catalog/templates.
Scaffold planning, rendering, and transactional application are separate tested concerns.
/scaffold parsing, completions, supported kinds—including primitive—previews, generated bytes/paths, containment, rollback, and errors remain compatible.
pi-catalog contains no generation templates or scaffolding claims and retains compatible runtime discovery behavior.
Generated inventories and focused/full repository qualification pass with independent review.

assessment.reason: The ownership move is conceptually direct, but the 374-line scaffolder combines security-sensitive transactions with rendering and many golden outputs; byte and rollback compatibility require disciplined tests.
unknowns: Some generated inventory fixtures may embed template paths not obvious from source references.
Git history-preserving moves depend on the final file mapping discovered during implementation.

practices.reason: Every scaffold kind and failure path must be frozen before moving templates or splitting code.
Planning, rendering, and application should separate without introducing a new cross-extension dependency.
Resource discovery, generated inventories, public commands, and security need integrated and independent evidence.

obligations.text: Run golden preview/apply and negative transaction tests for every scaffold kind, including primitive, containment, symlink, collision, partial failure, rollback, completions, and unusual names before migration.

Verify history-preserving template relocation, zero old-path references, distinct planning/rendering/application modules, unchanged generated bytes, unchanged primitive scaffolding, and unchanged catalog discovery.

Regenerate/check inventories and run scaffold, catalog, typecheck, resource, command, performance, and full repository gates, then obtain independent review of ownership, compatibility, and transaction safety.

work.title: Characterize all scaffold outputs and transaction behavior

testing.approach: Capture golden bytes/trees and negative planning/application behavior for every supported kind before moving files.
testing.reason: Template and module moves must be demonstrably behavior-neutral.

work.title: Move templates to pi-commands and split the scaffolder

testing.approach: Move templates, update bounded path resolution, extract planning/rendering/application modules, and rerun goldens plus catalog tests.
testing.reason: This corrects inverted ownership while reducing the scaffolder's concentration of concerns.

work.title: Refresh inventories and qualify commands/catalog ownership

testing.approach: Check for stale paths, regenerate inventories, run complete gates, and obtain independent source-bound review.
testing.reason: Repository resource metadata and public compatibility must agree with the new ownership.

decisions.text: Templates move beside pi-commands rather than into a new scaffolding package.
decisions.basis: It is the smallest ownership correction and avoids creating another package for one current consumer.

decisions.text: Retain /scaffold primitive unchanged for this initiative set; source-plan removal/deprecation is deferred.
decisions.basis: No release-level breaking-change approval exists, and the coordination authority explicitly preserves generated scaffold bytes and public behavior.

decisions.text: Run this work in the same post-provider wave as initiatives 04 and 05 when capacity permits.
decisions.basis: The consolidation plan treats UI, publication, and scaffolding migrations as separable rollback surfaces.

risks.text: Template relocation changes generated bytes or paths.
risks.mitigation: Use per-kind golden previews and applied-tree comparisons.

risks.text: Splitting transactional code weakens rollback or containment.
risks.mitigation: Keep adversarial application tests and separate pure planning/rendering from mutation.

risks.text: Stale resource/inventory paths survive the move.
risks.mitigation: Run repository-wide old-path checks and regenerate capability fixtures.
